specification:
## Goals
- Provide grid-sampled patch iteration over an image dataset. A separate patch generator supplies patch geometry, each patch can receive a per-patch transform, and each patch can carry its location in the source image (issue 1500).
- Keep patch generation (`PatchIter`) separate from dataset iteration (`GridPatchDataset`), so another generator can be supplied without changing the dataset class.
- Keep all grid geometry in the existing `iter_patch` utility, the single source of patch coordinates.

## Scope
- In scope: `monai/data/grid_dataset.py` (new `PatchIter`, reworked `GridPatchDataset`, float alias fix in the `PatchDataset` docstring example), `monai/data/utils.py` (`iter_patch` output and docstring), `monai/data/__init__.py` (export), `docs/source/data.rst` (autodoc entry), and a new `tests/test_grid_dataset.py`.
- Out of scope: `PatchDataset` behavior, `iter_patch_slices`, `get_valid_patch_size`, and `apply_transform`, apart from the `set_rnd` fix under Reliability.

## Assumptions
- Each image item is a channel-first array-like. The channel is always yielded whole, and patch sizes exclude it.
- The image dataset supports `len()`. Iterable-only datasets are not supported.
- The patch transform accepts a single patch array.
- A custom patch generator accepts one image item at a time. `GridPatchDataset` does not inspect item types.

## Terminology
- Image item: one element returned by indexing the image dataset.
- Patch: a sub-region of one image item with the full channel extent and the requested spatial size, taken from a padded copy so border patches are valid.
- Patch generator: a callable that takes one image item and returns an iterable of tuples. The first element is the patch; the second, if present, is its coordinate array. Further elements are ignored. `PatchIter` is the built-in generator.
- Coordinates: an integer array with one row per dimension, channel included, giving the start and stop of that dimension in the original unpadded frame.

## Workflows
Patch generation (`PatchIter`, once per image item):
- Prepend a "whole dimension" entry for the channel to the spatial patch size.
- Delegate to `iter_patch` with copy-back disabled, the start position unchanged, and the padding mode and options unchanged. Yield each tuple unchanged.

Dataset iteration (`GridPatchDataset`):
- Index range: 0 to the length of the image dataset. Inside a data-loader worker, split the range so each index goes to exactly one worker: per_worker is the ceiling of length divided by the worker count, and worker k takes indices from k times per_worker up to the smaller of (k plus 1) times per_worker and the length. Outside a worker, use the full range.
- For each index, fetch the image item and iterate the patch generator over it.
- Apply the transform to the patch alone (when set). If `with_coordinates` is false, yield only the patch; otherwise yield (transformed patch, coordinates).

## Data model
- Patch: a spatial sub-array with the whole channel dimension, a view into a padded copy, so in-place changes do not write back to the image.
- Coordinates: an integer array of shape (dimensions including channel, 2). Row i is [start_i, stop_i] in the original frame. The channel row is [0, C]. Stop can exceed the image extent for border patches.
- Dataset element: a patch when `with_coordinates` is false, or a (patch, coordinates) pair otherwise. Coordinates must be a numeric array, not a tuple of slice objects, so the default collation can batch them.

## API contracts
`PatchIter` (public, exported from `monai.data`):
- Options: `patch_size` (sequence of ints; 0 or None selects the whole dimension; the channel is excluded and its whole-channel entry is added internally). `start_pos` (sequence giving a position in the full channel-first array, so its first entry refers to the channel; default empty, meaning 0 in every dimension), normalized to a tuple on construction. `mode` (default wrap; accepts a NumpyPadMode member or its string value). Keyword padding options are forwarded to NumPy padding. Construction does no image work.
- Invocation: takes one image item and returns an iterable of (patch, coordinates) tuples, as produced by `iter_patch`.

`GridPatchDataset` (public, subclass of the torch IterableDataset):
- Constructor parameters, in order: `dataset`, `patch_iter` (required), `transform` (optional, default none), `with_coordinates` (default true).
- Must not accept `patch_size`, `start_pos`, `mode`, or padding options.

`iter_patch` (existing public utility, same name):
- Input parameters are unchanged. Each yielded item becomes a (patch view, coordinate array) pair instead of the patch alone. It is the only place that knows the padding offsets used for coordinates.

Package exports: `monai.data` exports `PatchIter` alongside `GridPatchDataset` and `PatchDataset`.

## Implementation constraints
- `GridPatchDataset` takes the patch generator as an injected callable and must not hard-code `iter_patch`.
- Do not reimplement padding, slicing, grid stepping, or coordinate offsets in the grid dataset module, build a parallel grid path, or depend on `iter_patch` internal padded offsets.
- Normalize `start_pos` in `PatchIter` with the existing `ensure_tuple` helper from the utilities package. Do not hand-roll it: `ensure_tuple` keeps a string and a zero-dimensional tensor as single values, which a plain tuple conversion does not.
- Apply the transform through the existing `apply_transform` helper with its map-items behavior disabled, so the transform receives one patch.
- Each image item is a single image. Do not iterate over channels or zip multiple arrays in lockstep.
- Asymmetry: the channel entry is prepended to `patch_size` only. `start_pos` never receives a channel entry from `PatchIter`; it is interpreted against the full array, exactly as `iter_patch` interprets it.
- Annotate the padding-options parameter as a `Dict` mapping, as the original constructor and the reference do.
- Do not add new public names for coordinate helpers to the utility module.
- `grid_dataset` may use torch (IterableDataset, worker info), NumPy (ceiling for the worker split), the base dataset class, `iter_patch`, `apply_transform`, and `NumpyPadMode` and `ensure_tuple` from the utilities package. The utility module must not import the grid dataset module. No new third-party dependencies.

## Validation
- `iter_patch` validates patch size and start position: 0 or None selects the whole dimension, sizes larger than the image are clipped, a short start position is padded with zeros at the end, and a long one is truncated.
- Do not add silent fallbacks for generator output arity. A generator yielding one element while coordinates are requested fails by unpacking.

## Error handling
- An image dataset without length raises NotImplementedError with the exact message "image dataset must implement `len()`." (ending with a period). Do not change the wording.
- An invalid mode propagates the conversion error from NumpyPadMode during `PatchIter` construction.
- Transform exceptions propagate through `apply_transform`, which wraps them as RuntimeError. Do not swallow them, and do not catch exceptions raised by the patch generator.

## Documentation
- Each edited module and the new test module keeps the repository's 10-line Apache license header verbatim.
- `GridPatchDataset` class docstring: explain grid sampling through a patch generator plus a per-patch transform, with a usage example (single-channel images, a `PatchIter` with patch size and start position, a per-patch intensity transform, a two-worker data loader). State the resulting patch shape and coordinate format. The example must match actual outputs.
- `GridPatchDataset` constructor docstring: document each parameter. `patch_iter` must yield tuples whose first element is the patch and second is the coordinates; reference `PatchIter`.
- `PatchIter` class docstring: a short summary only. Argument descriptions go in the constructor docstring's Args section, laid out as the `GridPatchDataset` constructor's is. A Note there states that the channel is excluded from patch size, with a worked example for a one-channel 3D image. Start position is a position in the full channel-first array.
- `iter_patch` docstring: the Yields section describes each item as a patch view paired with its coordinate array. Its Note gives the coordinate format, including the channel.
- Docstring examples must count the channel in dimensionality. A channel-first array of shape (1, 4, 4) is a one-channel 2D image with three dimensions, so its coordinates have three rows.
- Docstring prose and code lines stay within 120 characters, including indentation.
- `PatchDataset` docstring example: replace the deprecated NumPy float alias with the builtin float.
- `docs/source/data.rst`: add a `PatchIter` autodoc entry with members, in the same heading style as surrounding entries.

## Reliability
- Worker partitioning assigns each index to exactly one worker, with no index skipped or repeated.
- The `set_rnd` seeding helper, when recursing into object attributes, skips attribute names starting with a double underscore.

## Maintainability
- Lines are at most 120 characters in every edited module, including the test module. Format new and edited Python as the repository's black configuration would at line length 120.
- Every import in each edited module must be used. Remove imports that only replaced code used, including `math`. No duplicate imports.
- Edits are limited to the regions the feature needs. Unrelated lines, including license headers and existing imports, are preserved verbatim.

## Compatibility
- Intentional breaking change: the old `GridPatchDataset` constructor form (`patch_size`, `start_pos`, `mode`, padding options) is removed. Callers move to `PatchIter`. Do not add a shim.
- Behavior changes: each dataset item is a single image; coordinates are yielded by default; `iter_patch` callers receive (patch, coordinates) pairs.
- Additive: the `PatchIter` export. `PatchDataset` is unaffected.

## Operations
- Environment: Python 3.9 with the repository installed in editable mode and pytest available. Verify by running pytest on `tests/test_grid_dataset.py`.

## Behavioral acceptance criteria
1. With a custom generator yielding (item, index) tuples over string items and `with_coordinates` false, a data loader with batch size 3 yields contiguous chunks whose union has the same total length as the input.
2. Two single-channel 4x4 images, `PatchIter` with patch size 2x2 and start position (0, 0), and a per-patch RandShiftIntensity with offset 1.0 and probability 1.0 under seed 1234: a data loader with batch size 2 yields patch batches of shape (2, 1, 2, 2), and the data loader batches the coordinates without error.
3. For each 4x4 image, the four patches in visit order have coordinate arrays of shape (3, 2). The channel row is [0, 1]. The spatial rows, in order, are (0-2, 0-2), (2-4, 0-2), (0-2, 2-4), (2-4, 2-4), listed as (dimension 1 range, dimension 2 range).
4. The transform receives a single patch array of shape (channel, height, width), never a tuple. With no transform, patches pass through unchanged.
5. On non-Windows platforms, a two-worker data loader yields the same number of batches, and its final batch has the same coordinates as the single-process final batch.
6. An image dataset without length raises NotImplementedError with the exact message in Error handling.
7. For a channel-first array with more than two dimensions, a start position of (0, 4, 4, 4) on a one-channel 20x20x20 image yields the same patch grid as passing it to `iter_patch` directly.

## Test requirements
- `tests/test_grid_dataset.py`, class `TestGridPatchDataset`, containing `test_shape` and `test_loading_array` (the FAIL_TO_PASS tests).
- The custom generator used by `test_shape` is a module-scope function, not nested, local, or a lambda, because the spawn start method (the macOS default) pickles the dataset for the two-worker DataLoader.
- `setUp` sets determinism with seed 1234. `tearDown` resets determinism to none.
- `test_shape`: string items, a module-level generator yielding one (character, index) tuple per character of each item, `with_coordinates` false, batch size 3. Use 0 workers on Windows and 2 elsewhere. Compare sorted output and total length.
- `test_loading_array`: two 1x4x4 float images, `PatchIter` 2x2 with start position (0, 0), and RandShiftIntensity with offset 1.0 and probability 1.0. Call `set_determinism` with seed 1234 once, at the start of the test, before constructing the transform, generator, dataset, or any loader. Do not call it again.
- Single-process block (0 workers): check every batch shape as (2, 1, 2, 2). For the final batch, check patch values and coordinates. Expected patch values: first patch rows (1.7413, 2.7413) and (5.7413, 6.7413); second patch rows (9.1419, 10.1419) and (13.1419, 14.1419). Expected coordinates: first patch channel [0, 1], dimension 1 [0, 2], dimension 2 [2, 4]; second patch channel [0, 1], dimension 1 [2, 4], dimension 2 [2, 4]. Patch values use relative tolerance 1e-5 with no absolute tolerance; coordinates are compared exactly.
- Two-worker block (non-Windows only): runs immediately after the single-process block in the same test, reusing the same dataset, transform, and generator objects. Do not seed again or rebuild those objects between blocks: a zero-worker DataLoader construction draws a seed from the global random state and reseeds the dataset components.
- Two-worker block: check every batch shape as (2, 1, 2, 2). For the final batch, check coordinates against the single-process coordinates, and check patch values with a relative tolerance of 1e-3 against their own pinned values: first patch rows (2.3944, 3.3944) and (6.3944, 7.3944); second patch rows (10.6551, 11.6551) and (14.6551, 15.6551). Do not compare two-worker values with single-process values.
- Do not hand-seed a second transform instance or call `set_random_state` on the transform between constructing the single-process DataLoader and iterating it.
- Missing-length error assertions must use a literal substring check on the exception text, not assertRaisesRegex, because the message contains regex metacharacters.
- Test code follows the Maintainability rules.

What I removed or merged:
- Module architecture section: its ownership statements repeated Goals, Scope, and Workflows; the one unique fact (the docs autodoc placement) moved into Scope and Documentation.
- Dependencies section: folded into one bullet under Implementation constraints.
- Terminology "Grid sampling" bullet: stepping and visit order are fixed by Workflows and acceptance criterion 3.
- Reliability bullet about views not writing back: duplicated Data model's patch definition.
- Validation bullet on mode conversion: duplicated API contracts and Error handling.
- Acceptance criteria: merged the two data-loader checks (batch shape and coordinate batching) into criterion 2; dropped the "importable from monai.data" criterion, which the Package exports line already states.
- Test requirements: merged the two expected-value paragraphs into their blocks, shortened the seeding rationale, and removed the restatement that grid tests must not go in test_patch_dataset.py (the file path is already fixed in the requirement).
- Wordy phrasing shortened throughout (for example "Input parameters are unchanged" and "Constructor parameters, in order").

What I kept verbatim in meaning: all numeric expected values, the exact NotImplementedError message, the ensure_tuple rationale, the worker-split arithmetic, the channel asymmetry for start_pos, the Dict annotation, the no-shim and breaking-change rule, the seed-once and no-reseed rules, the literal substring assertion, the 120-column limits, and the import and license rules. The remaining text is sufficient for a correct implementation because each removed item was either a duplicate of a kept statement or restated acceptance criteria that still appear.
